items.title: Binary correlation models: setting-indexed tables of two-valued outcome laws, marginals and the CHSH functional
items.statement:
## Definition

This item fixes finite combinatorial vocabulary for outcome laws of a
two-station comparison. No physical interpretation, measurement model,
dynamics or locality assertion is made here; the physical readings are fixed
on the page of this pair. No choice principle is used.

**(a) Binary correlation model.** Let $I$ and $J$ be finite nonempty sets, the
**setting labels** of the two stations, and put
$\Sigma:=\{-1,+1\}$ for the common **outcome labels**. A **binary correlation
model** on $(I,J)$ is a family
$$\mu=(\mu_{ij})_{(i,j)\in I\times J},\qquad \mu_{ij}:\Sigma\times\Sigma\to[0,1],$$
of functions with the normalization
$$\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=1 \qquad\text{for every }(i,j)\in I\times J$$
([[def-finite-sum]]). Each $\mu_{ij}$ is the **joint law** of the setting pair
$(i,j)$: it is the outcome-weight function of a finite probability space on
the four outcomes $\Sigma\times\Sigma$ in the sense of
[[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]], and sums over $\Sigma\times\Sigma$
are finite sums.

**(b) Marginals.** For $(i,j)\in I\times J$ the **marginal law of the first
station** and the **marginal law of the second station** are
$$\mu^{A}_{ij}(\varepsilon):=\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta), \qquad \mu^{B}_{ij}(\delta):=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta), \qquad \varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma .$$

**(c) No-signalling.** The model $\mu$ is **no-signalling** when the marginal
law of the first station does not depend on the distant setting,
$\mu^{A}_{ij}=\mu^{A}_{ij'}$ for all $i\in I$ and all $j,j'\in J$, and the
marginal law of the second station does not depend on the distant setting,
$\mu^{B}_{ij}=\mu^{B}_{i'j}$ for all $j\in J$ and all $i,i'\in I$. The word is
used as a name for this pair of identities about the tables; no spatial or
causal claim is attached to it.

**(d) Correlations and the CHSH functional.** Assume $I=J=\{0,1\}$. The
**correlation** of the setting pair $(i,j)$ and the **CHSH functional** of the
model are the real numbers
$$E_{ij}(\mu):=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma} \varepsilon\,\delta\,\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta), \qquad S(\mu):=E_{00}(\mu)+E_{01}(\mu)+E_{10}(\mu)-E_{11}(\mu).$$

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) introduce finite tables, their marginals, the
no-signalling identities and one linear functional of four correlations. They
assert no physical assumption, no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law
for a real apparatus and no statement about nature; the identification of a
laboratory arrangement with a model $\mu$ is a separate physical matter.

items.title: Local-response representations of a binary correlation model: one setting-independent specification space and per-station response laws
items.statement:
## Definition

Let $\mu$ be a binary correlation model on the finite setting sets $I,J$ with
outcome labels $\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$
([[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]). No choice principle is used in
this definition.

**(a) Local-response representation.** A **local-response representation** of
$\mu$ is a tuple consisting of a probability space $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},
\mathbb P)$ ([[def-measure-space]], [[def-probability-measure]]) and two
families of **response laws**
$$(\alpha_{i})_{i\in I},\qquad (\beta_{j})_{j\in J},$$
where for each $i\in I$ the function
$\alpha_{i}:\Lambda\times\Sigma\to[0,1]$ has the two properties
$$\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)=1\quad(\lambda\in\Lambda), \qquad \lambda\mapsto\alpha_{i}(\lambda,+1)\ \text{is measurable}$$
([[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]), and the family
$(\beta_{j})_{j\in J}$ has the same two properties; and the **representation
identity**
$$\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\int_{\Lambda}\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)\,\beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)\, d\mathbb P(\lambda) =\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}\!\left[\alpha_{i}(\cdot,\varepsilon)\, \beta_{j}(\cdot,\delta)\right]$$
holds for every $(i,j)\in I\times J$ and every
$(\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma$. The integrand is a product of two
bounded measurable $[0,1]$-valued functions, so the expectation exists as a
finite number ([[def-expectation-of-a-nonnegative-or-integrable-random-variable]],
[[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]). The functions
$\alpha_{i}(\cdot,-1)=1-\alpha_{i}(\cdot,+1)$ and likewise for $\beta_{j}$ are
measurable as well. The variable $\lambda$ is called the **specification**
of the representation; it is a mathematical index, and no physical
interpretation is asserted.

**(b) Response functions (deterministic form).** A local-response
representation **has response functions** when there are measurable maps
$a_{i}:\Lambda\to\Sigma$ $(i\in I)$ and $b_{j}:\Lambda\to\Sigma$ $(j\in J)$
with
$$\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)=\mathbf 1_{\{a_{i}=\varepsilon\}}(\lambda), \qquad \beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)=\mathbf 1_{\{b_{j}=\delta\}}(\lambda),$$
in which case the representation identity reads
$$\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\mathbb P\bigl(\{a_{i}=\varepsilon\}\cap\{b_{j}=\delta\}\bigr).$$
The deterministic form is a special case of clause (a): it is obtained by
setting the response laws to the Dirac laws at $a_{i}(\lambda)$ and
$b_{j}(\lambda)$. In this form one and the same specification space and the
same single-station functions $a_{i}$ and $b_{j}$ serve all four setting
pairs, and the response of a station depends on the specification and on that
station's own setting only.

**(c) Terminology.** The two mathematical features named by **local response**
are: (i) a single specification space carring the probability law used for
every setting pair (setting-independence), and (ii) per-station response laws
that do not depend on the distant station's setting. A model that admits such
a representation is also called a **local model** of the tables in the
literature; the representation is an existence statement about the tables and
asserts no determinism, no mechanism, no dynamics and no causal relation. In
particular clause (a) permits probabilistic responses and does not require
the response functions of clause (b).

**(d) Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) fix vocabulary. They assert no physical
assumption and no property of any laboratory arrangement; whether a declared
physical model of a comparison admits a representation of this form is a
mathematical question about its tables, and the physical reading of that
question is fixed on the page of this pair.

items.title: Local-response representability implies setting-independent marginals
items.statement:
## Statement

Let $\mu$ be a binary correlation model on finite setting sets $I,J$ with
outcome labels $\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$
([[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]), and suppose that $\mu$ admits a
local-response representation with response laws $(\alpha_{i})$, $(\beta_{j})$
and probability space $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P)$
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]). Then:

(a) for every $i\in I$ the marginal law of the first station satisfies
$$\mu^{A}_{ij}=\mu^{A}_{ij'}\qquad\text{for all }j,j'\in J,$$
and for every $j\in J$ the marginal law of the second station satisfies
$\mu^{B}_{ij}=\mu^{B}_{i'j}$ for all $i,i'\in I$; that is, $\mu$ is
no-signalling;

(b) consequently, if a binary correlation model is not no-signalling, then it
admits no local-response representation.

No physical assumption and no choice principle is used; the proposition is a
statement about the tables and their representation.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A binary correlation model $\mu$; a local-response representation $(\alpha_{i})_{i\in I}$, $(\beta_{j})_{j\in J}$ on $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P)$; setting labels $i\in I$, $j,j'\in J$; outcome labels $\varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma$.

[F1] The joint laws and marginals are the finite sums $\mu^{A}_{ij}(\varepsilon)=\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$ and $\mu^{B}_{ij}(\delta)=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$, and no-signalling means exactly the pair of setting-independence identities of clause (c) of [[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]; under the representation hypothesis the joint law is also given by the representation identity $\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}[\alpha_{i}(\cdot,\varepsilon)\beta_{j}(\cdot,\delta)]$ of clause (a) of [[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]].

[F2] Each $\beta_{j}(\lambda,\cdot)$ is a probability law on the two-point set $\Sigma$: $\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)=1$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$ and every $j\in J$ ([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]] clause (a)).

[F3] Expectation is linear: $\mathbb E[aX+bY]=a\mathbb E[X]+b\mathbb E[Y]$ for integrable real random variables $X,Y$ and scalars $a,b$ ([[cor-expectation-linearity-monotonicity-and-modulus-bound]], [[def-expectation-of-a-nonnegative-or-integrable-random-variable]]); by induction the identity extends to finite sums $\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}$ over the two-element set $\Sigma$ ([[def-finite-sum]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; sum the representation identity over the distant outcome label, use the normalization of the distant response law and the linearity of expectation, and read off the setting-independence.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [Marginal of the first station] Fix $i\in I$, $j\in J$ and $\varepsilon\in\Sigma$. By [F1] and the definition of the marginal, $\mu^{A}_{ij}(\varepsilon)=\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}[\alpha_{i}(\cdot,\varepsilon)\beta_{j}(\cdot,\delta)]=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}\bigl[\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\alpha_{i}(\cdot,\varepsilon)\beta_{j}(\cdot,\delta)\bigr]=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}\bigl[\alpha_{i}(\cdot,\varepsilon)\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\beta_{j}(\cdot,\delta)\bigr]=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}[\alpha_{i}(\cdot,\varepsilon)]$, where the second equality is the representation identity, the third is the finite linearity of [F3], and the last is the normalization of [F2]. The resulting expression involves $i$ and $\varepsilon$ only, so $\mu^{A}_{ij}(\varepsilon)=\mu^{A}_{ij'}(\varepsilon)$ for every $j'\in J$; as $(\varepsilon,i,j)$ were arbitrary this is the first-station half of (a). [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.2 [Marginal of the second station] The same computation with the roles of the two stations exchanged, summing this time over $\varepsilon\in\Sigma$ and using the normalization $\sum_{\varepsilon}\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)=1$ of [F2], gives $\mu^{B}_{ij}(\delta)=\sum_{\varepsilon}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}[\beta_{j}(\cdot,\delta)]$ for every $\delta\in\Sigma$, an expression free of $i$; hence $\mu^{B}_{ij}=\mu^{B}_{i'j}$ for all $i,i'\in I$, the second-station half of (a). [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Assembly and contrapositive] Steps 1.1 and 1.2 give the two setting-independence identities, which by [F1] is exactly no-signalling of $\mu$; this is (a). For (b), if a model admits a local-response representation then (a) makes it no-signalling, so a model that is not no-signalling admits none. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Direction of the implication.** Representability is a strictly stronger
  requirement than no-signalling: this proposition gives only the implication
  from representability to no-signalling. The converse fails, and the
  framework's singlet arrangement is an explicit failing case once its four
  tables violate the CHSH bound of the next item.
- **Reading.** The two identities are the statement that each station's
  outcome law is unaffected by the distant setting in the model. This is a
  property of the declared tables; it is not a statement about any laboratory
  procedure and it assumes no spatial or temporal structure.

references.title: N. Brunner, D. Cavalcanti, S. Pironio, V. Scarani and S. Wehner, 'Bell nonlocality', Reviews of Modern Physics 86 (2014) 419, Section II, PDF page 3: a marginal p(a|x) = sum over b of p(ab|xy) is independent of the distant setting y, and this is identified with the no-signalling property of the local decomposition

items.title: The CHSH bound for every binary correlation model admitting a local-response representation
items.statement:
## Statement

Let $\mu$ be a binary correlation model on the setting sets $I=J=\{0,1\}$
with outcome labels $\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$, with correlations $E_{ij}(\mu)$ and
CHSH functional $S(\mu)$ as in
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]] clauses (d), and suppose that
$\mu$ admits a local-response representation with response laws
$(\alpha_{i})_{i\in I}$, $(\beta_{j})_{j\in J}$ on a probability space
$(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P)$
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]). Then
$$\bigl|S(\mu)\bigr|\le 2 .$$
The statement is a theorem about the tables and their representation; it
asserts no measurement, no dynamics, no spatial or causal structure, and it
contains no physics. No choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A binary correlation model $\mu$ on $I=J=\{0,1\}$; a local-response representation with response laws $(\alpha_{i})$, $(\beta_{j})$ on $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P)$.

[F1] The correlations and the CHSH functional are the finite sums $E_{ij}(\mu)=\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma}\varepsilon\delta\,\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$ and $S(\mu)=E_{00}(\mu)+E_{01}(\mu)+E_{10}(\mu)-E_{11}(\mu)$ ([[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]] clause (d), [[def-finite-sum]]), and the representation identity $\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}[\alpha_{i}(\cdot,\varepsilon)\beta_{j}(\cdot,\delta)]$ holds for all $i,j,\varepsilon,\delta$ ([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]] clause (a)).

[F2] For every $i\in I$ the **local mean** $a_{i}(\lambda):=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\varepsilon\,\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)=\alpha_{i}(\lambda,+1)-\alpha_{i}(\lambda,-1)$ is a measurable function of $\lambda$ taking values in $[-1,1]$, because $\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\cdot)$ is a probability law on $\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$ ([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]] clause (a)); the same holds for $b_{j}(\lambda):=\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\delta\,\beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)$ ([[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]], [[def-finite-sum]]).

[F3] Expectation is linear on finite sums: for integrable real random variables $X_{\varepsilon}$ on $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P)$ and real coefficients $c_{\varepsilon}$, $\mathbb E[\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}c_{\varepsilon}X_{\varepsilon}]=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}c_{\varepsilon}\mathbb E[X_{\varepsilon}]$ ([[cor-expectation-linearity-monotonicity-and-modulus-bound]], [[def-expectation-of-a-nonnegative-or-integrable-random-variable]], [[def-finite-sum]]); it is monotone and satisfies $|\mathbb E[Y]|\le\mathbb E[|Y|]$ for integrable real $Y$ ([[cor-expectation-linearity-monotonicity-and-modulus-bound]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; rewrite each correlation as the integral of the product of the two local means, bound the integrand of the CHSH functional pointwise by $2$ on the interval $[-1,1]^{4}$, and integrate.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [Correlations through local means] Fix $(i,j)\in\{0,1\}^{2}$. By [F1] and [F3], $E_{ij}(\mu)=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\varepsilon\delta\,\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}[\alpha_{i}(\cdot,\varepsilon)\beta_{j}(\cdot,\delta)]=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}\bigl[\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\varepsilon\delta\,\alpha_{i}(\cdot,\varepsilon)\beta_{j}(\cdot,\delta)\bigr]=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}\bigl[\bigl(\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\varepsilon\,\alpha_{i}(\cdot,\varepsilon)\bigr)\bigl(\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\delta\,\beta_{j}(\cdot,\delta)\bigr)\bigr]=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}[a_{i}b_{j}]$ with the local means of [F2], the inner factorizations being the distributive law in $\mathbb R$ for the two-term sums over $\Sigma$. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.2 [Pointwise bound] Let $u,v,s,t\in[-1,1]$. Then $|s(u+v)+t(u-v)|\le|u+v|+|u-v|$ by the triangle inequality and $|s|,|t|\le1$. For real $u,v$ one has $|u+v|+|u-v|=2\max(|u|,|v|)$: if $|v|\le|u|$ then both $u+v$ and $u-v$ have the sign of $u$ (for $|v|\le|u|$ neither crosses $0$), so the sum is $|2u|=2\max(|u|,|v|)$, and the case $|v|>|u|$ is symmetric with the roles of $u$ and $v$ exchanged. Hence $|u+v|+|u-v|\le2$, and the bound is $|s(u+v)+t(u-v)|\le2$. [given, algebra]

2.1 [CHSH bound] By [F1], [F2] and step 1.1, $S(\mu)=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}[a_{0}b_{0}]+\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}[a_{0}b_{1}]+\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}[a_{1}b_{0}]-\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}[a_{1}b_{1}]=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}\bigl[a_{0}(b_{0}+b_{1})+a_{1}(b_{0}-b_{1})\bigr]$, the second equality by the linearity of [F3]; the four local means take values in $[-1,1]$ by [F2], so the pointwise bound of step 1.2 gives $\bigl|a_{0}(\lambda)(b_{0}(\lambda)+b_{1}(\lambda))+a_{1}(\lambda)(b_{0}(\lambda)-b_{1}(\lambda))\bigr|\le2$ for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$. The modulus bound and monotonicity of [F3] applied to this pointwise bound yield $|S(\mu)|\le\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}[2]=2$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, F2, F3, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Deterministic special case.** If the representation has response functions
  $a_{i},b_{j}:\Lambda\to\Sigma$ in the sense of clause (b) of
  [[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]], then the four compositions
  $a_{i}b_{j}$ are $\pm1$-valued random variables on one probability space and
  the present bound reduces to the classical CHSH inequality for such
  variables, which is also proved directly in
  [[lem-nrqm-composites-chsh-and-finite-sampling-law]] (a). The probabilistic
  form proved here is the general case: it does not assume determinism of the
  responses.
- **Sharpness.** The bound $2$ is not improvable for the class: the model
  $I=J=\{0,1\}$ with $\mu_{ij}$ the point mass at
  $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ with $\varepsilon=\delta=+1$ for all $(i,j)$ admits
  the deterministic representation with $a_{i}\equiv+1$, $b_{j}\equiv+1$ and
  has $S(\mu)=2$; reversing the sign of every $b_{j}$ gives $S(\mu)=-2$.

items.title: Conditioning on a setting-independent selection preserves local-response representability and the CHSH bound
items.statement:
## Statement

Let $\mu$ be a binary correlation model on finite setting sets $I,J$ with
outcome labels $\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$
([[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]), and suppose that $\mu$ admits a
local-response representation with response laws $(\alpha_{i})_{i\in I}$,
$(\beta_{j})_{j\in J}$ on a probability space
$(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P)$
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]). Let
$D\in\Sigma_{\Lambda}$ be a **selection event** with $\mathbb P(D)>0$, put
$$\mathbb P_{D}(A):=\frac{\mathbb P(A\cap D)}{\mathbb P(D)}\qquad(A\in\Sigma_{\Lambda})$$
for the **conditional probability measure** on $D$, and define the
**$D$-conditional tables**
$$\mu^{D}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta):=\frac{1}{\mathbb P(D)} \int_{\Lambda}\mathbf 1_{D}(\lambda)\,\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)\, \beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)\,d\mathbb P(\lambda)$$
for $(i,j)\in I\times J$ and $(\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma$. Then:

(a) $\mathbb P_{D}$ is a probability measure on $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda})$
and $\mu^{D}:=(\mu^{D}_{ij})$ is a binary correlation model on $(I,J)$;

(b) the same response laws represent $\mu^{D}$ over $\mathbb P_{D}$:
$$\mu^{D}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\int_{\Lambda}\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)\,\beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)\, d\mathbb P_{D}(\lambda)\qquad\text{for all }i,j,\varepsilon,\delta ;$$

(c) if $I=J=\{0,1\}$, then $\bigl|S(\mu^{D})\bigr|\le2$.

The selection event $D$ is a subset of the specification space: membership in
$D$ is the same for every setting pair and does not depend on the settings or
on the outcomes. No choice principle is used.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A binary correlation model $\mu$; a local-response representation $(\alpha_{i})_{i\in I}$, $(\beta_{j})_{j\in J}$ on $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P)$; a selection event $D$ with $\mathbb P(D)>0$; the measures $\mathbb P_{D}$ and tables $\mu^{D}$ displayed in the statement.

[F1] The representation identity $\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P}[\alpha_{i}(\cdot,\varepsilon)\beta_{j}(\cdot,\delta)]$ holds, the response laws are $[0,1]$-valued with $\sum_{\varepsilon}\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)=1=\sum_{\delta}\beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)$ for every $\lambda$, and $\lambda\mapsto\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)$, $\lambda\mapsto\beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)$ are measurable ([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]] clause (a)); a binary correlation model is a family of normalized $[0,1]$-valued tables ([[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]] clause (a)).

[F2] $\mathbb P$ is a measure with $\mathbb P(\Lambda)=1$: it is countably additive on pairwise disjoint families and finitely additive, and $\mathbb P(\varnothing)=0$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]).

[F3] For an event $A$ the expectation of its indicator is its probability, $\mathbb E[\mathbf 1_{A}]=\mathbb P(A)$, and $\mathbf 1_{A}$ is measurable exactly when $A$ is ([[cor-expectation-of-an-indicator-is-probability]], [[prop-indicator-function-is-measurable-iff-its-set-is-measurable]], [[def-expectation-of-a-nonnegative-or-integrable-random-variable]]).

[F4] Expectation is linear on finite sums of nonnegative bounded measurable functions, $\mathbb E[\sum_{k}c_{k}f_{k}]=\sum_{k}c_{k}\mathbb E[f_{k}]$ for finite index sets and real coefficients $c_{k}\ge0$ ([[cor-expectation-linearity-monotonicity-and-modulus-bound]], [[def-finite-sum]]); in particular the finite sums over $\Sigma$ commute with the integral.

[F5] Every nonnegative measurable $f$ is the pointwise limit of an increasing sequence $(s_{k})$ of nonnegative simple functions with $0\le s_{k}\le s_{k+1}\le f$ ([[thm-nonnegative-measurable-functions-admit-increasing-simple-approximations]]); for such a sequence and any measure $\nu$, $\int s_{k}\,d\nu\uparrow\int f\,d\nu$ ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]); the integral of a nonnegative simple function is defined as its finite weighted sum ([[def-integral-of-a-nonnegative-simple-function]]).

[F6] If $\mu$ admits a local-response representation on $I=J=\{0,1\}$, then $|S(\mu)|\le2$ ([[thm-nrqm-bell-local-representations-satisfy-chsh]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; verify that conditioning on a measurable selection event gives a probability measure, prove the change-of-measure identity between $\mathbb P_{D}$ and $\mathbb P$ by the indicator-simple-monotone-convergence ladder, and apply it to the bounded response products.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [$\mathbb P_{D}$ is a probability measure] Since $\mathbb P(D)>0$, the definition of $\mathbb P_{D}$ is meaningful; it is nonnegative and $\mathbb P_{D}(\Lambda)=\mathbb P(\Lambda\cap D)/\mathbb P(D)=1$. For pairwise disjoint $A_{n}\in\Sigma_{\Lambda}$ with union $A$, the sets $A_{n}\cap D$ are pairwise disjoint with union $A\cap D$, so countable additivity of $\mathbb P$ [F2] gives $\mathbb P_{D}(A)=\mathbb P(A\cap D)/\mathbb P(D)=\sum_{n}\mathbb P(A_{n}\cap D)/\mathbb P(D)=\sum_{n}\mathbb P_{D}(A_{n})$; hence $\mathbb P_{D}$ is a probability measure on $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda})$. [given, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Indicators] Let $A\in\Sigma_{\Lambda}$. Then $\mathbf 1_{D}\mathbf 1_{A}=\mathbf 1_{A\cap D}$, and [F3] applied to the probability space $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P)$ gives $\int\mathbf 1_{D}\mathbf 1_{A}\,d\mathbb P=\mathbb E[\mathbf 1_{A\cap D}]=\mathbb P(A\cap D)$, while [F3] applied to $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P_{D})$ gives $\int\mathbf 1_{A}\,d\mathbb P_{D}=\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{D}}[\mathbf 1_{A}]=\mathbb P_{D}(A)=\mathbb P(A\cap D)/\mathbb P(D)$; hence $\int_{\Lambda}\mathbf 1_{A}\,d\mathbb P_{D}=\mathbb P(D)^{-1}\int_{\Lambda}\mathbf 1_{D}\mathbf 1_{A}\,d\mathbb P$. [given, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Nonnegative simple functions] By [F4] and the definition of the integral of a nonnegative simple function, both sides of the identity of step 2.1 are linear in the integrand over finite nonnegative combinations; hence for every nonnegative simple function $s$ on $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda})$ one has $\int_{\Lambda}s\,d\mathbb P_{D}=\mathbb P(D)^{-1}\int_{\Lambda}\mathbf 1_{D}s\,d\mathbb P$. [step 2.1, F4, algebra]

3.2 [Normalization] By [F1] and [F4], $\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}\mu^{D}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=\mathbb P(D)^{-1}\int\mathbf 1_{D}\bigl(\sum_{\varepsilon}\alpha_{i}(\cdot,\varepsilon)\bigr)\bigl(\sum_{\delta}\beta_{j}(\cdot,\delta)\bigr)d\mathbb P=\mathbb P(D)^{-1}\int\mathbf 1_{D}\,d\mathbb P=\mathbb P(D)/\mathbb P(D)=1$, the last equality by the indicator identity of step 2.1 with $A=\Lambda$, and each $\mu^{D}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)\ge0$ by nonnegativity of the integrand; hence $\mu^{D}$ is a binary correlation model on $(I,J)$. Together with step 1.1 this is (a). [step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Bounded measurable functions] Let $f\ge0$ be measurable and bounded, say $0\le f\le M<+\infty$. By [F5] choose an increasing sequence $(s_{k})$ of nonnegative simple functions with $s_{k}\uparrow f$; then $\mathbf 1_{D}s_{k}\uparrow\mathbf 1_{D}f$, and monotone convergence [F5] applied to the measures $\mathbb P_{D}$ and $\mathbb P$ gives $\int s_{k}\,d\mathbb P_{D}\uparrow\int f\,d\mathbb P_{D}$ and $\int\mathbf 1_{D}s_{k}\,d\mathbb P\uparrow\int\mathbf 1_{D}f\,d\mathbb P$. Passing to the limit in the identity of step 3.1, valid for every $k$, yields $\int_{\Lambda}f\,d\mathbb P_{D}=\mathbb P(D)^{-1}\int_{\Lambda}\mathbf 1_{D}f\,d\mathbb P$. [step 3.1, F5, algebra]

5.1 [Representation over $\mathbb P_{D}$] Fix $i,j,\varepsilon,\delta$ and put $f:=\alpha_{i}(\cdot,\varepsilon)\beta_{j}(\cdot,\delta)$. By [F1] $f$ is a product of two measurable $[0,1]$-valued functions, hence measurable and bounded with $0\le f\le1$. Step 4.1 gives $\int f\,d\mathbb P_{D}=\mathbb P(D)^{-1}\int\mathbf 1_{D}f\,d\mathbb P=\mu^{D}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$ by the definition of the $D$-conditional tables; this is (b). [given, F1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 [Bound and assembly] Step 5.1 exhibits a local-response representation of $\mu^{D}$ with the same response laws over the probability space $(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P_{D})$; hence [F6] applies to $\mu^{D}$ and gives $|S(\mu^{D})|\le2$ when $I=J=\{0,1\}$, which is (c). Steps 1.1 and 3.2 prove (a) and step 5.1 proves (b). [step 1.1, step 3.2, step 5.1, F6] ∎

## Remarks

- **Setting-independent selection.** The lemma conditions on an event of the
  specification space alone. This is the mathematical form of a
  **setting-independent selection**: whether a run enters the recorded sample
  is determined by the specification and not by the settings or the outcomes.
  Nothing is claimed here for selection rules that depend on the distant
  setting, on the local setting or on the observed outcomes; those require
  their own models and are not covered by the lemma.
- **Direction of use.** The lemma is used in the converse direction of
  detection: if the full tables of a comparison admit a local-response
  representation and the recorded trials are the runs that pass a
  setting-independent selection, then the recorded tables again admit one, so
  the CHSH bound holds for the recorded tables too. Without such a selection
  model no transfer of the bound to a sub-ensemble is asserted.

items.title: Singlet pairings: the joint laws of the two spin-half factors along two directions
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis
of the tensor construction cited below. Let $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ carry the
orthonormal basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$ and let
$$\sigma_{x}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_{y}=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\ i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_{z}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$
be the Pauli matrices of clause (e) of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] in the ordered basis
$(e_{+},e_{-})$; for $a=(a_{x},a_{y},a_{z})\in\mathbb R^{3}$ put
$\sigma_{a}:=a_{x}\sigma_{x}+a_{y}\sigma_{y}+a_{z}\sigma_{z}$, and for
$\varepsilon\in\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$ put
$$P_{a,\varepsilon}:=\tfrac12\bigl(I+\varepsilon\,\sigma_{a}\bigr).$$
Let $V\widehat\otimes V$ be the completed tensor product with inclusion
$\kappa$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] and let
$$\Psi:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\Bigr)\in V\widehat\otimes V, \qquad q:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})+\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\Bigr).$$
Then:

(a) for every unit $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and $\varepsilon\in\Sigma$ the
operator $P_{a,\varepsilon}$ is an orthogonal projection on $V$,
$P_{a,+}+P_{a,-}=I$ and
$P_{a,\varepsilon}P_{a,\varepsilon'}=\delta_{\varepsilon\varepsilon'}P_{a,\varepsilon}$;

(b) $\|\Psi\|=1$ and the four vectors $\Psi,q,\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{+}),
\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{-})$ are mutually orthogonal, so
$(\Psi,q,\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{+}),\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{-}))$ is an
orthonormal basis of $V\widehat\otimes V$;

(c) for all unit $a,b\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and all
$\varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma$,
$$\bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle =\tfrac14\bigl(1-\varepsilon\delta\,a\cdot b\bigr);$$

(d) the marginals of the four numbers in (c) are
$$\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle=\tfrac12 =\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle,$$
and their correlation is
$$\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\varepsilon\,\delta\, \bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle =-a\cdot b .$$

The lemma is a finite-dimensional computation in the tensor product; it
asserts no preparation, measurement or physical interpretation. The Axiom of
Countable Choice enters only through the construction of the completed tensor
product cited from [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]].

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The space $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ with orthonormal basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$ and the Pauli matrices $\sigma_{x},\sigma_{y},\sigma_{z}$; unit vectors $a,b\in\mathbb R^{3}$; the completed tensor product $V\widehat\otimes V$ with inclusion $\kappa$; the vectors $\Psi$ and $q$; the labels $\varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma$; the Axiom of Countable Choice.

[F1] The Pauli matrices satisfy $\sigma_{i}^{*}=\sigma_{i}$, $\sigma_{x}^{2}=\sigma_{y}^{2}=\sigma_{z}^{2}=I$, $\sigma_{x}\sigma_{y}=i\sigma_{z}$, $\sigma_{y}\sigma_{z}=i\sigma_{x}$, $\sigma_{z}\sigma_{x}=i\sigma_{y}$ and consequently $\sigma_{i}\sigma_{j}+\sigma_{j}\sigma_{i}=2\delta_{ij}I$; their actions on the basis are $\sigma_{x}e_{+}=e_{-}$, $\sigma_{x}e_{-}=e_{+}$, $\sigma_{y}e_{+}=ie_{-}$, $\sigma_{y}e_{-}=-ie_{+}$, $\sigma_{z}e_{+}=e_{+}$ and $\sigma_{z}e_{-}=-e_{-}$ ([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]).

[F2] For every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ the matrix $\sigma_{a}=\sum_{i}a_{i}\sigma_{i}$ is self-adjoint and $\sigma_{a}^{2}=\sum_{i,j}a_{i}a_{j}\sigma_{i}\sigma_{j}=\sum_{i}a_{i}^{2}I+\sum_{i\ne j}a_{i}a_{j}\sigma_{i}\sigma_{j}=\|a\|^{2}I$ by the anticommutation relations of [F1]; in particular $\sigma_{a}^{2}=I$ for unit $a$, and $\sigma_{a}$ is a linear map $V\to V$ ([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clauses (a), (e), [[def-linear-map]]).

[F3] The completed tensor product $V\widehat\otimes V$ is a complex Hilbert space, $\kappa$ is a linear isometry with dense image, $\langle\kappa(u\otimes v),\kappa(u'\otimes v')\rangle=\langle u,u'\rangle\langle v,v'\rangle$ for all $u,u',v,v'\in V$, and the four elementary tensors $\kappa(e_{\varepsilon}\otimes e_{\delta})$ form an orthonormal basis ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clauses (b), (c), (d), [[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]).

[F4] For bounded $S,T$ on $V$ there is a bounded operator $S\otimes T$ on $V\widehat\otimes V$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa(Su\otimes Tv)$ for all $u,v\in V$, $(S\otimes T)^{*}=S^{*}\otimes T^{*}$, and the assignment is linear in each argument ([[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clauses (a), (b), (c)); consequently computations on $\Psi$ may be performed term by term in the orthonormal basis of [F3].

[F5] In a complex inner product space, $|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\|$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]]); the norm is induced by the inner product, $\|z\|=\langle z,z\rangle^{1/2}$ ([[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; verify the projection algebra from the Pauli anticommutation relations, compute the action of the local and product Pauli operators on the four product-basis vectors, read the pairings off the orthonormal basis, and assemble the joint numbers from the projection decomposition.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Projections] Fix a unit $a$ and $\varepsilon\in\Sigma$. By [F2], $P_{a,\varepsilon}^{*}=\tfrac12(I+\varepsilon\sigma_{a}^{*})=\tfrac12(I+\varepsilon\sigma_{a})=P_{a,\varepsilon}$ and $P_{a,\varepsilon}^{2}=\tfrac14(I+2\varepsilon\sigma_{a}+\varepsilon^{2}\sigma_{a}^{2})=\tfrac14(2I+2\varepsilon\sigma_{a})=\tfrac12(I+\varepsilon\sigma_{a})=P_{a,\varepsilon}$ using $\varepsilon^{2}=1$ and $\sigma_{a}^{2}=I$; hence $P_{a,\varepsilon}$ is an orthogonal projection. Moreover $P_{a,+}+P_{a,-}=I$ and $P_{a,+}P_{a,-}=\tfrac14(I-\sigma_{a}^{2})=0$, which is (a). [given, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Orthonormal basis] By [F3], $\|\Psi\|^{2}=\tfrac12(\|e_{+}\otimes e_{-}\|^{2}+\|e_{-}\otimes e_{+}\|^{2})=1$ and $\|q\|^{2}=1$, and the inner products pair the four displayed vectors as $0$ or $1$: for instance $\langle\Psi,q\rangle=\tfrac12(1-1)=0$ and $\langle\Psi,\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{+})\rangle=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\bigl(\langle e_{+},e_{+}\rangle\langle e_{-},e_{+}\rangle-\langle e_{-},e_{+}\rangle\langle e_{+},e_{+}\rangle\bigr)=0$ by the product formula of [F3]. Since the four elementary tensors already form an orthonormal basis of the four-dimensional space $V\widehat\otimes V$, so do the four mutually orthogonal unit vectors $\Psi,q,\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{+}),\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{-})$; this is (b). [given, F3, F5, algebra]

2.1 [Local Pauli operators on $\Psi$] Using [F1] and [F4] term by term, $(\sigma_{z}\otimes I)\Psi=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})+\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\bigr)=q$ and $(I\otimes\sigma_{z})\Psi=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\bigl(-\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\bigr)=-q$; further $(\sigma_{x}\otimes I)\Psi=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\bigl(\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{+})\bigr)$, $(I\otimes\sigma_{x})\Psi=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{+})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{-})\bigr)$, $(\sigma_{y}\otimes I)\Psi=\tfrac{i}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{+})+\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{-})\bigr)$ and $(I\otimes\sigma_{y})\Psi=\tfrac{-i}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{+})+\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{-})\bigr)$, all of which are linear combinations of the three basis vectors $q,\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{+}),\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{-})$ orthogonal to $\Psi$ by step 1.2; hence $\langle(\sigma_{i}\otimes I)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=0=\langle(I\otimes\sigma_{i})\Psi,\Psi\rangle$ for $i=x,y,z$, and by the linearity of [F4] in the first tensor argument, $\langle(\sigma_{a}\otimes I)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=0=\langle(I\otimes\sigma_{b})\Psi,\Psi\rangle$ for all $a,b$. [given, F1, F4, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 [Product Pauli operators on $\Psi$] Term-by-term application of [F1] and [F4] gives $(\sigma_x\otimes\sigma_x)\Psi=(\sigma_y\otimes\sigma_y)\Psi=(\sigma_z\otimes\sigma_z)\Psi=-\Psi$. Put $r_+:=(\kappa(e_+\otimes e_+)+\kappa(e_-\otimes e_-))/\sqrt2$ and $r_-:=(\kappa(e_+\otimes e_+)-\kappa(e_-\otimes e_-))/\sqrt2$. The six mixed products are $(\sigma_x\otimes\sigma_y)\Psi=-iq$, $(\sigma_y\otimes\sigma_x)\Psi=iq$, $(\sigma_x\otimes\sigma_z)\Psi=-r_+$, $(\sigma_z\otimes\sigma_x)\Psi=r_+$, $(\sigma_y\otimes\sigma_z)\Psi=ir_-$ and $(\sigma_z\otimes\sigma_y)\Psi=-ir_-$. Each is orthogonal to $\Psi$ by step 1.2. Thus $\langle(\sigma_i\otimes\sigma_j)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=-\delta_{ij}$ for all $i,j\in\{x,y,z\}$. [given, F1, F4, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Directional correlation] By the linearity of [F4], $(\sigma_{a}\otimes\sigma_{b})\Psi=\sum_{i,j}a_{i}b_{j}(\sigma_{i}\otimes\sigma_{j})\Psi$, so the final identity of step 2.2 and the conjugate-linearity of the inner product in its second argument give $\langle(\sigma_{a}\otimes\sigma_{b})\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\sum_{i,j}a_{i}b_{j}(-\delta_{ij})=-a\cdot b$, with real $a,b$. [step 2.2, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Joint numbers] Let $a,b$ be unit vectors and $\varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma$. By step 1.1, $P_{a,\varepsilon}=\tfrac12(I+\varepsilon\sigma_{a})$ and $P_{b,\delta}=\tfrac12(I+\delta\sigma_{b})$, so multilinearity of the tensor product [F4] and the bilinearity of the inner product give $\bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle=\tfrac14\bigl(\langle\Psi,\Psi\rangle+\varepsilon\langle(\sigma_{a}\otimes I)\Psi,\Psi\rangle+\delta\langle(I\otimes\sigma_{b})\Psi,\Psi\rangle+\varepsilon\delta\langle(\sigma_{a}\otimes\sigma_{b})\Psi,\Psi\rangle\bigr)=\tfrac14(1-\varepsilon\delta\,a\cdot b)$ by steps 1.2, 2.1 and 3.1; this is (c). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, F4, algebra]

5.1 [Marginals and correlation] Summing the formula of step 4.1 over the distant label and using $\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\delta=0$ gives $\sum_{\delta}\bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle=\tfrac14(2-\varepsilon a\cdot b\cdot0)=\tfrac12$, and symmetrically for the other marginal; the correlation is $\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}\varepsilon\delta\,\tfrac14(1-\varepsilon\delta a\cdot b)=\tfrac14\bigl((\sum_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon)(\sum_{\delta}\delta)-a\cdot b\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}(\varepsilon\delta)^{2}\bigr)=\tfrac14(0-4\,a\cdot b)=-a\cdot b$; this is (d). [step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 [Assembly] Step 1.1 is (a), step 1.2 is (b), step 4.1 is (c) and step 5.1 is (d); only the finite-dimensional tensor calculus of [F1]-[F4] and real arithmetic were used, and no physical interpretation is asserted. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Relation to the framework's singlet.** The vector $\Psi$ is the singlet of
  the two-factor spin-half model; its joint numbers (c) are the pairings of the
  local spin projections, and (d) shows that each single-station marginal is
  $\tfrac12$ and that the directional correlation is $-a\cdot b$. The physical
  reading of these numbers as outcome laws of a declared preparation is fixed
  on the page of this pair; this lemma itself is linear algebra.
- **No degenerate directions.** The computation covers every pair of unit
  directions, including $a=b$ (correlation $-1$) and $a=-b$ (correlation
  $+1$) and $a\perp b$ (correlation $0$); the joint numbers are
  $\tfrac14(1\mp\varepsilon\delta)$ in these cases and remain in $[0,1]$.

## Definition

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3, the
internal-factor assignment of the identical-particle and spin postulate P6 and
the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), together with the
composite, observable and measurement readings of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], the
angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] and the
units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared spin-half factors.** A **declared spin-half factor** is the
internal factor $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ of the spin-$s$ model
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with spin label
$s=\tfrac12$, with its orthonormal basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$, the self-adjoint
matrices $J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) and the spin
observables $S_{i}:=\hbar J_{i}$, read as assigned sharp observables with unit
$\mathrm{J\,s}$ by clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] and P6
clause (ii). For a unit direction $n\in\mathbb R^{3}$ put
$S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$. By
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] clause (c) the
observable $S_{n}$ has the two eigenvalues $\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}$ with
spectral projections
$$P_{n,\varepsilon}:=\tfrac12\bigl(I+\varepsilon\,n\cdot\sigma\bigr), \qquad \varepsilon\in\Sigma=\{-1,+1\},$$
and the label $\varepsilon$ attached to the projection $P_{n,\varepsilon}$ is
the **sign label** of the outcome; the outcome coordinate is
$\varepsilon\hbar/2$, read in the unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, while the sign label
itself is dimensionless.

**(b) Declared arrangement.** A **declared spin correlation arrangement**
consists of: the declared composite $V\widehat\otimes V$ of two declared
spin-half factors, with inclusion $\kappa$, in the sense of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] (a
declared pair of distinguishable subsystems whose assigned spaces are the two
internal factors); a **declared preparation** $\rho\in D(V\widehat\otimes V)$,
the set of density operators on the composite
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]); and two unit
**setting directions** $a_{0},a_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ for the first station and
$b_{0},b_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ for the second station. The setting labels are
$I=J=\{0,1\}$.

**(c) Declared local sign measurements.** For the first station and setting
$i\in I$, the **declared local sign measurement** is the declared ideal sharp
measurement whose outcome structure is the pair
$(P_{a_{i},+}\otimes I,\;P_{a_{i},-}\otimes I)$ with the sign labels $\pm1$:
these are the spectral projections of the local readout of the assigned
observable $(S_{a_{i}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ on the declared composite, the local
readout being constructed through the spectral measure by clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] and
[[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]]. The second station's
declared local sign measurement for setting $j$ is
$(I\otimes P_{b_{j},+},\;I\otimes P_{b_{j},-})$, defined symmetrically.

**(d) Declared joint sign measurement and tables.** For $(i,j)\in I\times J$
the **declared joint sign measurement** of the setting pair is the declared
ideal sharp measurement of the composite whose outcome structure is
$$E_{ij}:=\bigl(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta}\bigr)_{(\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma}, \qquad E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta},$$
with the pair of sign labels as its labels: by clause (c) of
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] each factor is an
orthogonal projection, and the tensor calculus of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] gives
$E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)E_{ij}(\varepsilon',\delta')=
\delta_{\varepsilon\varepsilon'}\delta_{\delta\delta'}E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$
and $\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=I$, so this is a
finite family of mutually orthogonal projections resolving the identity, as
required by clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]. Its
**outcome law** in the declared preparation $\rho$ is
$$\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)\bigr), \qquad (\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma,$$
read from clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
(compare P2 clause (ii), [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]).
The **correlation table of the arrangement** is the family
$\nu^{\rho}=(\nu^{\rho}_{ij})_{(i,j)\in I\times J}$, which is a binary
correlation model on $(I,J)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]] clause (a); its correlations
$E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho})$, its marginals and its CHSH functional $S(\nu^{\rho})$ are
the ones of clauses (b) and (d) of that definition, and are written
$S(\rho;a_{0},a_{1};b_{0},b_{1})$ when the arrangement data are displayed.

**(e) Declared local-response models of the arrangement.** A **declared
local-response model of the arrangement** is a local-response representation,
in the sense of [[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]], of the
correlation table $\nu^{\rho}$. It is a model of the same four tables: it
consists of a probability space of **specifications** and of per-station
response laws, subject to the representation identity, and it need not be a
model of the framework's state space. The arrangement **admits a
local-response model** when such a representation exists.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix model vocabulary. They assign no spatial
position, worldline, spatial separation or temporal order to the two factors;
they assert no dynamics, no interaction, no apparatus, no detection procedure
and no measured correlation; they do not assert that the composite is prepared
by any particular laboratory procedure. Whether a laboratory arrangement
realizes the declared preparation, the declared directions and the declared
sign measurements is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this
definition; the model's assignments of states to preparations and of spectral
projections to quantities are the readings of P1, P2 and P3 fixed on the
earlier pages.

## Remarks

- **Why the joint measurement is declared and not derived.** The framework's
  measurement vocabulary declares outcome structures; it does not assert that
  arbitrary observables of two factors possess a joint sharp measurement. For
  the arrangement the product family of clause (d) is itself a finite family
  of mutually orthogonal projections resolving the identity, so the joint
  measurement of the two sign measurements is a declared ideal sharp
  measurement of the composite in the framework's own sense. No claim is made
  that an arbitrary pair of laboratory procedures realizes it.
- **Sign labels versus coordinates.** The sign labels $\pm1$ are the outcome
  indices used by the correlation tables; the physical outcome coordinates are
  $\pm\hbar/2$ in the unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$. The correlation and the CHSH
  functional of clause (d) are functionals of the sign labels and are
  dimensionless; no numerical value of an angular momentum coordinate is
  asserted anywhere.

## Statement

Adopt the declared spin correlation arrangement of
[[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]]: the composite
$V\widehat\otimes V$ of two declared spin-half factors with orthonormal basis
$(e_{+},e_{-})$, a declared preparation $\rho\in D(V\widehat\otimes V)$, the
setting directions $a_{0},a_{1},b_{0},b_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and the four
declared joint sign measurements with outcome laws
$$\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta})\bigr), \qquad P_{a,\varepsilon}=\tfrac12(I+\varepsilon\,a\cdot\sigma) .$$
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the hypotheses of
the cited suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), and
take the **singlet preparation**
$$\Psi:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\Bigr), \qquad \rho_{\Psi}:=T_{\Psi,\Psi},$$
where $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ is the rank-one operator of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]. Then:

(a) for every $(i,j)\in\{0,1\}^{2}$ and all $\varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma$,
$$\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\bigl\langle(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle =\tfrac14\bigl(1-\varepsilon\delta\,a_{i}\cdot b_{j}\bigr);$$

(b) the correlations of the arrangement are
$E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-a_{i}\cdot b_{j}$ and
$$S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}) =-\bigl[a_{0}\cdot b_{0}+a_{0}\cdot b_{1}+a_{1}\cdot b_{0}-a_{1}\cdot b_{1}\bigr] =-\,(a_{0}\cdot(b_{0}+b_{1})+a_{1}\cdot(b_{0}-b_{1}));$$
in particular, for the unit directions
$a_{0}=(0,0,1)$, $a_{1}=(1,0,0)$, $b_{0}=(1,0,1)/\sqrt2$ and
$b_{1}=(-1,0,1)/\sqrt2$ one has $S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-2\sqrt2$, so
$\bigl|S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})\bigr|=2\sqrt2>2$;

(c) consequently the correlation table $\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}$ of the arrangement
at those directions admits no local-response model in the sense of clause (e)
of [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]]: there is no local-response
representation of the four tables
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]) with these laws;

(d) the marginal sign laws of the arrangement are
$\nu^{\rho_{\Psi},A}_{ij}(\varepsilon)=\tfrac12=
\nu^{\rho_{\Psi},B}_{ij}(\delta)$ for every setting pair and every direction, so
the table is no-signalling in the sense of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]; and a discarded declared local
instrument on either factor leaves the reduced preparation of the other factor
and every local outcome law of that factor unchanged
([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] clause (b)).

The item is a conditional model computation: it asserts no measured
correlation, no apparatus and no empirical fact, and its exclusion is exactly
of the declared local-response class of these four tables. Higher singleton
claims about hidden variables in general are not asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The declared spin correlation arrangement with the singlet preparation $\rho_{\Psi}$; setting directions $a_{0},a_{1},b_{0},b_{1}$; the test directions $a_{0}=(0,0,1)$, $a_{1}=(1,0,0)$, $b_{0}=(1,0,1)/\sqrt2$, $b_{1}=(-1,0,1)/\sqrt2$; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice.

[F1] The arrangement's outcome law is $\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta}))$, its correlations and CHSH functional are the ones of the binary correlation model $\nu^{\rho}$, and its local-response models are the local-response representations of $\nu^{\rho}$ ([[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]] clauses (d), (e), [[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]] clauses (b), (d)).

[F2] For unit $a,b$ the pairings of the singlet are $\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\tfrac14(1-\varepsilon\delta\,a\cdot b)$ and the associated marginal sums are $\tfrac12$ and the correlation is $-a\cdot b$ ([[lem-nrqm-bell-singlet-pairings]] clauses (b), (c), (d)).

[F3] For a unit vector $w$ and a bounded operator $B$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(T_{w,w}B)=\langle Bw,w\rangle$: $T_{w,w}B=T_{w,B^{*}w}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (b), (d)); the singlet preparation $\rho_{\Psi}=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ is a pure density operator with $\|\Psi\|=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clauses (a), (b), [[lem-nrqm-bell-singlet-pairings]] clause (b)).

[F4] If a binary correlation model on $I=J=\{0,1\}$ admits a local-response representation, then $|S|\le2$ ([[thm-nrqm-bell-local-representations-satisfy-chsh]]).

[F5] A discarded declared local instrument of one factor of a declared composite leaves the reduced preparation of the other factor unchanged, and hence every local outcome law of that factor ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] clause (b)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; evaluate the pure preparation pairing with the rank-one trace identity, read the directional numbers off the singlet pairings, compute the specified-angle value of the CHSH combination, and apply the CHSH bound for representable models.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Outcome laws] For every $(i,j)$ and $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ the measurement reading [F1] and the trace identity [F3] give $\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=\operatorname{tr}(T_{\Psi,\Psi}(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta}))=\langle(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta})\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\tfrac14(1-\varepsilon\delta\,a_{i}\cdot b_{j})$ by [F2]; this is (a). [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Correlations and CHSH combination] By [F1], [F2] and step 1.1, $E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}\varepsilon\delta\,\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=-a_{i}\cdot b_{j}$, so $S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=E_{00}+E_{01}+E_{10}-E_{11}=-[a_{0}\cdot b_{0}+a_{0}\cdot b_{1}+a_{1}\cdot b_{0}-a_{1}\cdot b_{1}]=-[a_{0}\cdot(b_{0}+b_{1})+a_{1}\cdot(b_{0}-b_{1})]$, the last equality by bilinearity of the Euclidean pairing. [given, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 [Marginals and no-signalling] Summing the formula of step 1.1 with [F2] gives $\nu^{\rho_{\Psi},A}_{ij}(\varepsilon)=\tfrac14(1-\varepsilon a_{i}\cdot b_{j})+\tfrac14(1+\varepsilon a_{i}\cdot b_{j})=\tfrac12$ for both values of $\varepsilon$, independent of $j$, and symmetrically $\nu^{\rho_{\Psi},B}_{ij}(\delta)=\tfrac12$ independent of $i$; hence the table is no-signalling. The discarded-instrument statement is [F5]. This is (d). [step 1.1, F2, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Specified directions] For $a_{0}=(0,0,1)$, $a_{1}=(1,0,0)$, $b_{0}=(1,0,1)/\sqrt2$, $b_{1}=(-1,0,1)/\sqrt2$ one has $a_{0}\cdot b_{0}=a_{0}\cdot b_{1}=a_{1}\cdot b_{0}=1/\sqrt2$ and $a_{1}\cdot b_{1}=-1/\sqrt2$; substituting into step 2.1 gives $S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-[1/\sqrt2+1/\sqrt2+1/\sqrt2+1/\sqrt2]=-4/\sqrt2=-2\sqrt2$, so $|S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})|=2\sqrt2>2$. This is the second part of (b). [given, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [No local-response model] If the four tables $\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}$ at the specified directions admitted a local-response representation, then [F4] would give $|S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})|\le2$, contradicting step 3.1; hence no such representation exists, which is (c) at those directions. [step 3.1, F4, algebra]

5.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 is (a), steps 2.1 and 3.1 are (b), step 4.1 is (c) and step 2.2 is (d). Only the declared arrangement, the singlet pairings, the rank-one trace identity and the CHSH bound for representable models were used; no measurement, apparatus, spatial separation or recorded data entered, and the exclusion is only of the declared local-response class of these four tables. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **The value $2\sqrt2$ is the largest possible for this arrangement.** The
  general bound $|S|\le2\sqrt2$ over every preparation and every choice of
  directions is proved as [[pthm-nrqm-bell-tsirelson-bound-for-arrangements]];
  the present computation shows that the singlet at the displayed directions
  attains it.
- **What is excluded.** The four tables of the arrangement do not admit a
  representation by one setting-independent specification space with
  per-station response laws. The computation does not address models of these
  tables outside that class, and it makes no claim that any laboratory
  procedure realizes the arrangement or that any measured correlation agrees
  with $\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}$.

items.title: Tsirelson bound for every declared spin correlation arrangement of the framework
items.statement:
## Statement

Let $(V\widehat\otimes V,\rho,a_{0},a_{1},b_{0},b_{1})$ be a declared spin
correlation arrangement of the two declared spin-half factors in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]], with a preparation
$\rho\in D(V\widehat\otimes V)$, unit directions
$a_{i},b_{j}\in\mathbb R^{3}$, outcome laws
$\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$ and CHSH functional
$S(\nu^{\rho})$ as in clauses (d) of that definition and (d) of
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematical
suppliers. Then:

(a) $\bigl|S(\nu^{\rho})\bigr|\le2\sqrt2$ for every preparation $\rho$ and all
unit directions $a_{0},a_{1},b_{0},b_{1}$;

(b) the bound is attained: with $\Psi:=\frac1{\sqrt2}(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+}))$
and the singlet preparation $\rho_{\Psi}=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$, for the directions
$a_{0}=(0,0,1)$, $a_{1}=(1,0,0)$, $b_{0}=(1,0,1)/\sqrt2$,
$b_{1}=(-1,0,1)/\sqrt2$ one has
$S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-2\sqrt2$, so
$\bigl|S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})\bigr|=2\sqrt2$.

The statement is a conditional theorem about the declared arrangement model; it
asserts no measured value and no apparatus realization.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A declared spin correlation arrangement with preparation $\rho$ and directions $a_{0},a_{1},b_{0},b_{1}$; the outcome laws $\nu^{\rho}_{ij}$ and their CHSH functional; the Axiom of Countable Choice.

[F1] The arrangement's outcome law is $\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta}))$ with $P_{a,\varepsilon}=\tfrac12(I+\varepsilon a\cdot\sigma)$; the correlations are $E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho})=\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}\varepsilon\delta\,\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$ and $S(\nu^{\rho})=E_{00}+E_{01}+E_{10}-E_{11}$ ([[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]] clauses (a), (d), [[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]] clause (d)).

[F2] The Pauli matrix $\sigma_{a}=\sum_{i}a_{i}\sigma_{i}$ for unit $a$ is a self-adjoint involution, $\sigma_{a}^{2}=I$, and $P_{a,+}-P_{a,-}=\sigma_{a}$ ([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]] clause (a)).

[F3] The completed tensor product $V\widehat\otimes V$ carries the bounded tensor calculus: $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$, $(S\otimes T)^{*}=S^{*}\otimes T^{*}$, $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$, and the assignment is linear in each argument ([[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F4] A density operator $\rho$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ and $\|\rho\|_{1}=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a), [[def-trace-class-operator]]).

[F5] Trace class is a two-sided Banach operator ideal: for trace-class $T$ and bounded $A,B$ one has $ATB$ trace class with $\|ATB\|_{1}\le\|A\|\,\|T\|_{1}\|B\|$, and $\|T\|\le\|T\|_{1}$ ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1, 2); the trace is linear on the trace class and $|\operatorname{tr}T|\le\|T\|_{1}$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

[F6] For bounded self-adjoint involutions $A_{0},A_{1}$ on a Hilbert space $H$ and $B_{0},B_{1}$ on a Hilbert space $K$, the operator $C:=A_{0}\otimes(B_{0}+B_{1})+A_{1}\otimes(B_{0}-B_{1})$ on $H\widehat\otimes K$ is self-adjoint with $\|C\|\le2\sqrt2$; equivalently, for every unit vector $\psi$ the CHSH combination of the expectations $\langle(A_{i}\otimes B_{j})\psi,\psi\rangle$ is at most $2\sqrt2$ in absolute value ([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-tsirelson-bound]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F7] For the singlet preparation and the displayed directions, $S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-2\sqrt2$ ([[texp-nrqm-bell-singlet-arrangement-contrast]] clause (b)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; write the CHSH functional as the trace of the preparation against the CHSH operator, apply the operator-norm bound of the finite-dimensional Tsirelson theorem, and bound the trace by the ideal and trace inequalities.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F7].

1.1 [CHSH functional as an operator trace] Put $C:=\sigma_{a_{0}}\otimes(\sigma_{b_{0}}+\sigma_{b_{1}})+\sigma_{a_{1}}\otimes(\sigma_{b_{0}}-\sigma_{b_{1}})$, a bounded operator on $V\widehat\otimes V$ by [F3]. For each $(i,j)$, [F2] gives $\sigma_{a_{i}}\otimes\sigma_{b_{j}}=(P_{a_{i},+}-P_{a_{i},-})\otimes(P_{b_{j},+}-P_{b_{j},-})=\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}\varepsilon\delta\,P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta}$, a finite sum, so by [F1], the linearity of the finite sum and the linearity of the trace [F5], $E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho})=\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}\varepsilon\delta\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta}))=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}\varepsilon\delta(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta})\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\sigma_{a_{i}}\otimes\sigma_{b_{j}}))$. Summing the four terms with the CHSH signs and using [F3] and the linearity of the trace gives $S(\nu^{\rho})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\,C)$. [given, F1, F2, F3, F5, algebra]

1.2 [Operator norm bound] By [F2] the matrices $\sigma_{a_{i}},\sigma_{b_{j}}$ are self-adjoint involutions, so [F6] applies and gives $\|C\|\le2\sqrt2$. [given, F2, F6]

2.1 [Trace bound] By [F4] $\rho$ is trace class with $\|\rho\|_{1}=1$, so [F5] makes $\rho C$ trace class with $\|\rho C\|_{1}\le\|\rho\|_{1}\|C\|=\|C\|$, and the trace bound of [F5] gives $|\operatorname{tr}(\rho C)|\le\|\rho C\|_{1}\le\|C\|\le2\sqrt2$. With step 1.1 this is $\bigl|S(\nu^{\rho})\bigr|\le2\sqrt2$, which is (a). [step 1.1, step 1.2, F4, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Attainment] Clause (b) is exactly [F7] for the singlet preparation and the displayed directions, and step 2.1 shows that no value larger than $2\sqrt2$ occurs. [F7, step 2.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Sharpness within the declared class.** The bound cannot be lowered for the
  declared arrangement model, because the singlet at the displayed directions
  attains it (clause (b)). This is a statement about the declared binary sign
  measurements of the arrangement; it is not an optimality statement for other
  functionals, for more settings, for unsharp measurements or for other
  systems.
- **Where the bound is used.** The bound is one half of the contrast of this
  page: the CHSH functional of any representable model is at most $2$ in
  absolute value ([[thm-nrqm-bell-local-representations-satisfy-chsh]]), while
  the declared arrangement permits $2\sqrt2$; the gap is not a numerical
  coincidence of the singlet but a property of the framework's binary sharp
  readouts of self-adjoint involutions.

items.title: Measurement-model boundaries of the singlet-local comparison: what the no-go excludes and what it does not
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **What the comparison establishes.** For the declared spin correlation
  arrangement of [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]], the four sign
  tables are the laws $\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$ of clause (d) of
  that definition. If the arrangement's CHSH functional satisfies
  $|S(\nu^{\rho})|>2$, then the four tables admit no local-response model:
  every local-response representation would give $|S|\le2$ by
  [[thm-nrqm-bell-local-representations-satisfy-chsh]]. The singlet at the
  directions of [[texp-nrqm-bell-singlet-arrangement-contrast]] is the
  displayed instance, with $|S|=2\sqrt2$. The statement is a conditional
  no-go for one precisely defined class of models of one precisely defined set
  of four tables.

- **What is not excluded.** The theorem concerns models of the four tables
  that consist of one specification space whose probability law is the same
  for all setting pairs, together with per-station response laws that do not
  depend on the distant setting ([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]
  clauses (a), (c)). Models outside that class are not addressed: a model
  whose specification or response is allowed to depend on the distant setting,
  a model that does not reproduce all four tables simultaneously, or a model
  of a different arrangement or of a different measurement structure is not
  excluded. In particular the comparison does not rule out "hidden variables"
  in general, and it does not claim that no completion of quantum mechanics
  exists; it excludes the declared local-response class for these tables.

- **Assumptions used.** The deduction rests on the framework readings P1, P2,
  P3, P6 and P7 fixed by
  [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]], on the declared composite,
  preparation and spin-half assignments, on the ideal sharp character of the
  declared measurements ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]),
  and on the cited mathematics (the finite-dimensional tensor calculus, the
  CHSH bound for representable models and the operator bound of
  [[pthm-nrqm-bell-tsirelson-bound-for-arrangements]]). Changing one of these
  readings voids the conditional conclusion for the changed model; it does not
  weaken it, and a replacement conclusion needs its own proof.

- **Measurement-model boundary.** The declared sign measurements have exactly
  two outcomes with sign labels $\pm1$; detection efficiency, finite
  resolution, dark counts, background, drift and loss are outside the
  arrangement and require their own apparatus models. In particular an
  observed violation on a recorded sub-ensemble does not by itself contradict
  the declared model class: the recorded tables are conditional tables, and
  the CHSH bound transfers to them only when the selection is itself
  setting-independent, as in
  [[lem-nrqm-bell-setting-independent-selection-closure]]; that lemma is a
  sufficient condition and is not a claim about any real detector. Finite
  samples add a sampling model and its fluctuations, treated on the examples
  page, and no finite sample decides between the models with certainty.

- **No-signalling is not the separator.** Every local-response model is
  no-signalling ([[prop-nrqm-bell-local-representations-are-no-signalling]]),
  and the arrangement's marginals are also setting-independent
  ([[texp-nrqm-bell-singlet-arrangement-contrast]] clause (d)); a discarded
  declared local instrument on one factor leaves the other factor unchanged
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] clause (b)).
  The contrast between the two classes therefore lies in the joint tables,
  not in any dependence of one station's marginal law on the distant setting.

- **Attainment and sharpness.** The value $2\sqrt2$ is attained for the
  declared arrangement
  ([[pthm-nrqm-bell-tsirelson-bound-for-arrangements]] clause (b)), so within
  the declared class of binary sharp readouts of self-adjoint involutions no
  smaller uniform bound for the CHSH functional is available. This says
  nothing about other functionals, other numbers of settings, unsharp
  measurements or other systems.

- **Interpretation.** The result is a statement about four probability
  tables. It identifies no mechanism, no influence between the stations and
  no preferred frame; the arrangement carries no spatial or temporal
  structure. Interpretations that attach additional physical content to the
  violation are not part of the deduction and are not asserted here. Whether
  a laboratory arrangement realizes the declared model and what a recorded
  sample shows are separate matters under the preparation and apparatus
  postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the Bell-models page: conditional model results and the deferred experiment destination
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **What the page contains.** Mathematical vocabulary for binary correlation
  models and their local-response representations
  ([[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]],
  [[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]), the CHSH bound for every
  representable model ([[thm-nrqm-bell-local-representations-satisfy-chsh]]),
  the preservation of representability and of the bound under a
  setting-independent selection
  ([[lem-nrqm-bell-setting-independent-selection-closure]]), the exact joint
  laws of the two-factor singlet ([[lem-nrqm-bell-singlet-pairings]]), the
  declared spin correlation arrangement of the framework
  ([[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]]), the singlet computation with
  the failure of local-response representability at violating settings
  ([[texp-nrqm-bell-singlet-arrangement-contrast]]) and the Tsirelson bound
  with its attainment
  ([[pthm-nrqm-bell-tsirelson-bound-for-arrangements]]). All are conditional
  model statements.

- **What the page does not contain.** No experiment item, no reported count,
  no calibration, no detector efficiency, no loss model, no background, no
  trial-level uncertainty analysis, no p-value, no confidence level and no
  measured correlation. None of the computations establishes that the
  framework or any of its postulates describes nature, and none of them
  asserts that any laboratory procedure realizes the declared arrangement.
  The marginals, tables and correlations are model probabilities for the
  declared preparation; the identification of a concrete apparatus with the
  declared measurements, and of repetitions with a sampling model, is the
  tested identification with uncertainty of clause (iii) of the preparation
  and apparatus postulate P7
  ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

- **Deferred experiment destination.** The design of this pair reserves an
  experiment item for a Bell test. Such an item is not built here: it would
  require reading a primary or authoritative full report and recording its
  source-specific preparation and apparatus, calibration, measured outputs,
  trial count where reported, detection efficiency, loss and post-selection,
  background, the reported statistical treatment and systematics, and the
  source's omissions; none of the sources read for this page supplies that
  level of detail. The sources' experimental remarks motivate the model
  comparison only: Binney's section 6.1.4 refers to the 1972
  Freedman-Clauser test and cites a 1998 photonic test, and the MIT chapter
  closes with the statement that experiments have confirmed violations; no
  numerical value from those secondary accounts is reproduced here as an
  observation, and no interval, count or precision is asserted. The
  statistics and primary-report gap named in the design is recorded as an
  open destination.

- **Source qualifications not imported.** The same sources contain general
  conclusions that the comparison rules out hidden variables as such or that
  quantum mechanics cannot be superseded by a theory with a definite spin
  direction. Those conclusions are stronger than the conditional statement
  proved here — which excludes only the declared local-response class of the
  declared tables — and are not imported. Likewise the operator bound used on
  this page is proved by the operator-norm route of the cited mathematics
  (the identity for the square of the CHSH operator and the norm bound); no
  reversed variance inequality of the form
  $\langle C^{2}\rangle\le\langle C\rangle^{2}$ and no commutator estimate is
  used as a premise.

- **What a comparison with data could show.** Under the declared
  preparation, detection, settings and sampling models, agreement of recorded
  frequencies with the arrangement's tables would support the combined model
  and apparatus assumptions, and a recorded CHSH functional outside the bound
  of a declared representable model would exclude that model class only under
  those same detection and selection assumptions. Agreement is evidence about
  the combined assumptions, not a proof of the framework, and a null or
  reduced result does not by itself falsify it; the finite-sample and
  selection qualifications are stated on the examples page.

- **Interpretation and scope of the model.** The arrangement assigns no
  spatial positions, separation or temporal order to the two factors, so no
  relativistic locality principle is modelled here; the exclusion is a
  statement about the four tables. The boundaries of the comparison are
  recorded in [[rem-nrqm-bell-boundaries-and-comparison-scope]], and no
  interpretation of the violation beyond those boundaries is asserted.
