items.title: Worked Bell angles: the singlet against the EPR product mixture at the same directions
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the declared spin correlation arrangement of
[[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]] over the two declared spin-half
factors $V,V$ with basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$. Fix the orthonormal vectors
$e_{1}:=(1,0,0)$, $e_{2}:=(0,1,0)$, $e_{3}:=(0,0,1)$ and the four unit
directions
$$a_{0}:=e_{3},\qquad a_{1}:=e_{1},\qquad b_{0}:=\frac{e_{3}+e_{1}}{\sqrt2},\qquad b_{1}:=\frac{e_{3}-e_{1}}{\sqrt2}.$$
Consider two arrangements over these same directions:

- the **singlet arrangement**, with the singlet preparation
  $\rho_{\Psi}=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$,
  $\Psi=\frac1{\sqrt2}(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+}))$;
- the **product-mixture arrangement**, with the EPR-type mixture
  $$M:=\tfrac12\,T_{e_{+}\otimes e_{-},\,e_{+}\otimes e_{-}} +\tfrac12\,T_{e_{-}\otimes e_{+},\,e_{-}\otimes e_{+}} ,$$
  a convex combination of the two product preparations of definite opposite
  spins along $e_{3}$.

Then:

(a) for the singlet arrangement the four correlations are
$$E_{00}=E_{01}=E_{10}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt2},\qquad E_{11}=+\frac{1}{\sqrt2}, \qquad S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-2\sqrt2 ;$$

(b) for the product-mixture arrangement the four sign tables are
$$\nu^{M}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=\tfrac14\bigl(1-\varepsilon\delta\, (a_{i})_{3}(b_{j})_{3}\bigr),$$
so its correlations are $E_{ij}=- (a_{i})_{3}(b_{j})_{3}$; at the displayed
directions $(a_{0})_{3}=1$, $(a_{1})_{3}=0$ and
$(b_{0})_{3}=(b_{1})_{3}=1/\sqrt2$, hence
$$E_{00}=E_{01}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt2},\qquad E_{10}=E_{11}=0,\qquad S(\nu^{M})=-\sqrt2 ;$$

(c) the mixture's tables admit a local-response model
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]): on the two-point
specification space, the response laws
$$\alpha_{i}(1,\varepsilon)=\tfrac12(1+\varepsilon(a_{i})_{3}),\quad \alpha_{i}(2,\varepsilon)=\tfrac12(1-\varepsilon(a_{i})_{3}),\quad \beta_{j}(1,\delta)=\tfrac12(1-\delta(b_{j})_{3}),\quad \beta_{j}(2,\delta)=\tfrac12(1+\delta(b_{j})_{3})$$
with specification weights $\tfrac12,\tfrac12$ reproduce
$\nu^{M}$; consequently $\bigl|S(\nu^{M})\bigr|=\sqrt2\le2$, as the bound for
representable models requires
([[thm-nrqm-bell-local-representations-satisfy-chsh]]);

(d) both arrangements have the same marginal sign laws
$\nu^{A}(\pm)=\nu^{B}(\pm)=\tfrac12$ for every direction, and the same reduced
preparation $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}M=\tfrac12I=\operatorname{Tr}_{B}\rho_{\Psi}$
on each factor, although their joint tables and CHSH functionals differ:
$\bigl|S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})\bigr|=2\sqrt2>2\ge\sqrt2=\bigl|S(\nu^{M})\bigr|$.

All clauses are conditional computations in the declared framework; no
measured correlation is asserted.

## Verification

**Given:** The declared arrangements with the singlet preparation $\rho_{\Psi}$ and the mixture $M$; the four directions $a_{0}=e_{3}$, $a_{1}=e_{1}$, $b_{0}=(e_{3}+e_{1})/\sqrt2$, $b_{1}=(e_{3}-e_{1})/\sqrt2$; the spin-half projections $P_{a,\varepsilon}=\tfrac12(I+\varepsilon a\cdot\sigma)$.

[L1] The arrangement's outcome law is $\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta}))$ and its correlations and CHSH functional are read from [[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]] clause (d) ([[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]] clauses (a), (d)).

[L2] The singlet pairings and their marginals and correlation are $\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\tfrac14(1-\varepsilon\delta a\cdot b)$ with marginals $\tfrac12$ and correlation $-a\cdot b$ ([[lem-nrqm-bell-singlet-pairings]] clauses (b), (c), (d)); at the displayed directions the singlet's CHSH value is $-2\sqrt2$ ([[texp-nrqm-bell-singlet-arrangement-contrast]] clause (b)).

[L3] For a product preparation $T_{u\otimes v,u\otimes v}$ the joint law of the local sign measurements factorizes: $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u\otimes v,u\otimes v}(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta}))=\|P_{a,\varepsilon}u\|^{2}\|P_{b,\delta}v\|^{2}$ ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-statistics-of-products-and-entangled-preparations]] clause (a), [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (b), (d)); and for the spin-half basis states $\langle(n\cdot\sigma)e_{+},e_{+}\rangle=n_{3}$, $\langle(n\cdot\sigma)e_{-},e_{-}\rangle=-n_{3}$, so $\|P_{n,\varepsilon}e_{+}\|^{2}=\tfrac12(1+\varepsilon n_{3})$ and $\|P_{n,\varepsilon}e_{-}\|^{2}=\tfrac12(1-\varepsilon n_{3})$ ([[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] clause (c), [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e)).

[L4] The partial trace of a rank-one product operator is $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}T_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle T_{u,u'}$, and $\operatorname{tr}$ is linear on the trace class ([[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] clause (c), [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clause (b)).

[L5] Every binary correlation model admitting a local-response representation satisfies $|S|\le2$ ([[thm-nrqm-bell-local-representations-satisfy-chsh]]).

**Proof technique:** direct; evaluate the singlet numbers from the singlet pairings, compute the mixture's tables as the average of the two product tables, exhibit the two-specification representation and check its identity, and compare the marginals.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [L1]-[L5].

1.1 [Directions and singlet values] The four directions are unit vectors with $a_{0}\cdot b_{0}=a_{0}\cdot b_{1}=a_{1}\cdot b_{0}=1/\sqrt2$ and $a_{1}\cdot b_{1}=-1/\sqrt2$. By [L1] and [L2], $E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-a_{i}\cdot b_{j}$, so $E_{00}=E_{01}=E_{10}=-1/\sqrt2$, $E_{11}=+1/\sqrt2$ and $S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-2\sqrt2$; this is (a). [given, L1, L2, algebra]

1.2 [Product-state tables] Write $u_{+}:=e_{+}$, $u_{-}:=e_{-}$. By [L3], for the product preparation $T_{u_{\tau}\otimes u_{-\tau},u_{\tau}\otimes u_{-\tau}}$ (with $\tau=+$ or $-$) the joint sign law at $(i,j)$ is $\tfrac12(1+\varepsilon\tau(a_{i})_{3})\cdot\tfrac12(1-\delta\tau(b_{j})_{3})$. [given, L3, algebra]

2.1 [Mixture tables] By [L1] the outcome law of a convex mixture is the corresponding convex combination of the laws, so the two product tables of step 1.2 average to $\nu^{M}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=\tfrac14\bigl[\tfrac12(1+\varepsilon(a_{i})_{3})(1-\delta(b_{j})_{3})+\tfrac12(1-\varepsilon(a_{i})_{3})(1+\delta(b_{j})_{3})\bigr]=\tfrac14(1-\varepsilon\delta(a_{i})_{3}(b_{j})_{3})$; this is the table formula of (b). [step 1.2, L1, algebra]

3.1 [Mixture correlations and CHSH value] Summing the table of step 2.1 with the product signs gives $E_{ij}(\nu^{M})=-(a_{i})_{3}(b_{j})_{3}$; substituting $(a_{0})_{3}=1$, $(a_{1})_{3}=0$, $(b_{0})_{3}=(b_{1})_{3}=1/\sqrt2$ gives $E_{00}=E_{01}=-1/\sqrt2$ and $E_{10}=E_{11}=0$, hence $S(\nu^{M})=-1/\sqrt2-1/\sqrt2-0+0=-\sqrt2$; this completes (b). [step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 [Explicit representation] Choose a two-point specification space $\Lambda=\{1,2\}$ with weights $\mathbb P(\{1\})=\mathbb P(\{2\})=\tfrac12$ and define the response laws by the display of (c). Then for each $(i,j,\varepsilon,\delta)$ one has $\int_{\Lambda}\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon)\beta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)\,d\mathbb P(\lambda)=\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac12(1+\varepsilon(a_{i})_{3})\cdot\tfrac12(1-\delta(b_{j})_{3})+\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac12(1-\varepsilon(a_{i})_{3})\cdot\tfrac12(1+\delta(b_{j})_{3})=\tfrac14\bigl(1-\varepsilon\delta(a_{i})_{3}(b_{j})_{3}\bigr)=\nu^{M}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$ by step 2.1, so $(\alpha,\beta,\mathbb P)$ is a local-response representation of $\nu^{M}$; the bound $|S(\nu^{M})|\le2$ then follows from [L5] and is consistent with the value $-\sqrt2$ of (b), since $\sqrt2\le2$. This is (c). [step 2.1, L5, algebra]

4.1 [Common marginals and comparison] Summing the mixture table of step 2.1 over the distant label gives $\tfrac12$ for each local label, and the singlet's marginals are $\tfrac12$ by [L2]; the reduced preparations are $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}M=\tfrac12T_{e_{+},e_{+}}+\tfrac12T_{e_{-},e_{-}}=\tfrac12I$ and, expanding $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ in the product basis and applying [L4] linearly, $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}\rho_{\Psi}=\tfrac12(T_{e_{+},e_{+}}+T_{e_{-},e_{-}})=\tfrac12I$, so both arrangements share every single-station statistic while their CHSH functionals are $2\sqrt2$ and $\sqrt2$ in absolute value. This is (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, L2, L4, algebra]

5.1 [Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 3.2 and 4.1 prove (a)-(d); only the declared arrangements, the singlet pairings, the product-factorization theorem, the spin-half outcome laws, the partial trace and the CHSH bound for representable models were used, and no measured correlation is asserted. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Why the mixture does not distinguish the two routes.** The mixture's
  tables are represented by a probabilistic local-response model with two
  specifications, not by a deterministic response function of a single
  specification; this is why clause (a) of
  [[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]] is stated for response laws
  rather than for response functions. The singlet's tables at the displayed
  directions admit no representation of either form.
- **The lesson of the comparison.** Identical marginals and identical reduced
  preparations on both factors do not determine the joint tables: the
  contrast between $2\sqrt2$ and $\sqrt2$ is invisible to every single-station
  statistic and is a property of the correlations alone.

items.title: Finite samples of a declared arrangement: the CHSH estimator, its concentration and the limits of a finite-sample verdict
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt a declared spin correlation arrangement $(V\widehat\otimes V,\rho,
a_{0},a_{1},b_{0},b_{1})$ of [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]]
with its outcome laws $\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$, correlations
$E_{ij}=E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho})$ and CHSH functional
$S=S(\nu^{\rho})$. Let $n\ge1$ and declare the following **sampling model**
(the statistical model of clause (ii) of the preparation and apparatus
postulate P7, [[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]): on a
probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ let
$$\bigl(\Sigma_{ijk},\mathrm T_{ijk}\bigr)_{\substack{i,j\in\{0,1\}\\ k\in\{1,\dots,n\}}}$$
be $4n$ random elements with values in $\Sigma\times\Sigma$ that are
**mutually independent** and have the declared laws
$$\mathbb P\bigl((\Sigma_{ijk},\mathrm T_{ijk})=(\varepsilon,\delta)\bigr) =\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) \qquad\text{for every }i,j,k,\varepsilon,\delta$$
([[def-independence-of-finite-random-variables]],
[[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]). Define the **sample
correlations** and the **sample CHSH functional**
$$\widehat E_{ij}:=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{n}\Sigma_{ijk}\mathrm T_{ijk}, \qquad \widehat S:=\widehat E_{00}+\widehat E_{01}+\widehat E_{10}-\widehat E_{11}.$$
Then:

(a) $\mathbb E[\widehat E_{ij}]=E_{ij}$ and
$\operatorname{Var}(\widehat E_{ij})\le1/n$ for all $(i,j)$;

(b) $\mathbb E[\widehat S]=S$, $\operatorname{Var}(\widehat S)\le4/n$, and
for every $\varepsilon>0$
$$\mathbb P\bigl(|\widehat S-S|\ge\varepsilon\bigr)\le\frac{4}{n\varepsilon^{2}} ;$$

(c) threshold consequences: if the declared model satisfies
$S\le2-\varepsilon$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, then
$\mathbb P(\widehat S>2)\le4/(n\varepsilon^{2})$; if the declared model is
the singlet arrangement with $S=-2\sqrt2$ and
$\varepsilon:=2\sqrt2-2$, then
$\mathbb P(\widehat S\ge-2)\le4/(n\varepsilon^{2})$. Moreover, for every
declared acceptance criterion $C\subseteq(\Sigma\times\Sigma)^{4n}$ that
rejects at least one outcome sequence $(x_{ijk})$ with
$\prod_{i,j,k}\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(x_{ijk})>0$, the failure probability of the
criterion is at least $\prod_{i,j,k}\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(x_{ijk})>0$;

(d) scope: the independence, the identical distribution and the tables
$\nu^{\rho}$ are declared model assumptions of the sampling model, not
consequences of P1-P6; clauses (a)-(c) assert no measured count, no p-value,
no error rate, no power, no required sample size and no empirical conclusion.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A declared arrangement with tables $\nu^{\rho}_{ij}$, correlations $E_{ij}$ and CHSH functional $S$; the $4n$ mutually independent random elements $(\Sigma_{ijk},\mathrm T_{ijk})$ with the declared laws; the sample correlations $\widehat E_{ij}$ and the sample functional $\widehat S$; a declared criterion $C$.

[F1] The outcome laws, correlations and CHSH functional are the ones of clause (d) of [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]] and clauses (b), (d) of [[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]; the sampling model of the statement is an additional declared assumption in the sense of clause (ii) of [[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]] and is not implied by the framework's postulates.

[F2] A finite family of finite-valued random elements is mutually independent when the probability of every joint event factors as the product over the index set ([[def-independence-of-finite-random-variables]]); in particular every sequence of values with all one-run probabilities positive has probability equal to the product of those probabilities, which is positive ([[lem-nrqm-composites-chsh-and-finite-sampling-law]] clause (b)).

[F3] Expectation is linear, and for a finite family of integrable real random variables the expectation of the finite sum is the sum of the expectations ([[cor-expectation-linearity-monotonicity-and-modulus-bound]], [[def-expectation-of-a-nonnegative-or-integrable-random-variable]], [[def-finite-sum]]).

[F4] Variance is defined by $\operatorname{Var}(X)=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb E[X])^{2}]=\mathbb E[X^{2}]-\mathbb E[X]^{2}$ for a square-integrable real random variable, and $\operatorname{Var}(cX)=c^{2}\operatorname{Var}(X)$ ([[def-moments-variance-and-covariance]]); the variances of a finite pairwise-independent family add, $\operatorname{Var}(\sum_{l}X_{l})=\sum_{l}\operatorname{Var}(X_{l})$ ([[cor-variance-adds-for-pairwise-independent-random-variables]]).

[F5] For a square-integrable real random variable and $a>0$, $\mathbb P(|X-\mathbb E[X]|\ge a)\le\operatorname{Var}(X)/a^{2}$ ([[cor-chebyshev-inequality-for-random-variables]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; identify each sample correlation as a mean of independent bounded products, compute its mean and variance, add the four variances of the independent setting groups, apply Chebyshev, and read the positive-probability statement off the product law.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Mean and variance of one sample correlation] Fix $(i,j)$ and put $X_{k}:=\Sigma_{ijk}\mathrm T_{ijk}$ for $k=1,\dots,n$. Each $X_{k}$ takes values in $\{-1,+1\}$, so $\mathbb E[X_{k}]=\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}\varepsilon\delta\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=E_{ij}$ by [F1] and [F3], and $X_{k}^{2}=1$ identically, so $\operatorname{Var}(X_{k})=\mathbb E[X_{k}^{2}]-\mathbb E[X_{k}]^{2}=1-E_{ij}^{2}\le1$ by [F4]; the $X_{k}$ are mutually independent because the corresponding pairs are, and $\widehat E_{ij}=\frac1n\sum_{k}X_{k}$. Hence $\mathbb E[\widehat E_{ij}]=\frac1n\sum_{k}\mathbb E[X_{k}]=E_{ij}$ by [F3], and $\operatorname{Var}(\widehat E_{ij})=\frac{1}{n^{2}}\operatorname{Var}(\sum_{k}X_{k})=\frac{1}{n^{2}}\sum_{k}\operatorname{Var}(X_{k})\le\frac{n}{n^{2}}=\frac1n$ by [F4]; this is (a). [given, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

1.2 [Positive failure probability] Let $(x_{ijk})$ be a sequence of outcomes with $p:=\prod_{i,j,k}\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(x_{ijk})>0$. By mutual independence [F2] the event that the sample equals this sequence has probability exactly $p>0$; if the criterion $C$ rejects this sequence, that is $(x_{ijk})\notin C$, then the singleton event $\{(\Sigma_{ijk},\mathrm T_{ijk})=(x_{ijk})\}$ is contained in the failure event $\{(\Sigma_{ijk},\mathrm T_{ijk})\notin C\}$, so the failure probability is at least $p>0$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [CHSH estimator moments and concentration] The four families $\{X_{k}\}_{k}$ for the four setting pairs involve disjoint groups of the $4n$ mutually independent random elements, so the four estimators $\widehat E_{ij}$ are mutually independent; by [F3] and [F4], $\mathbb E[\widehat S]=E_{00}+E_{01}+E_{10}-E_{11}=S$ and $\operatorname{Var}(\widehat S)=\sum_{i,j}\operatorname{Var}(\widehat E_{ij})\le4\cdot\frac1n=\frac4n$ by step 1.1. Chebyshev [F5] applied to $\widehat S$ gives $\mathbb P(|\widehat S-S|\ge\varepsilon)\le\operatorname{Var}(\widehat S)/\varepsilon^{2}\le4/(n\varepsilon^{2})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$; this is (b). [step 1.1, F1, F3, F4, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Threshold events] If $S\le2-\varepsilon$ then $\{\widehat S>2\}\subseteq\{|\widehat S-S|\ge\varepsilon\}$, so its probability is at most $4/(n\varepsilon^{2})$ by step 2.1. For the singlet arrangement $S=-2\sqrt2$, so $-\!S=2\sqrt2$ and $\{\widehat S\ge-2\}\subseteq\{|\widehat S-S|\ge2\sqrt2-2\}$, giving the second bound. [step 2.1, F1, algebra]

4.1 [Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a) and (b), step 1.2 and step 3.1 prove the two parts of (c), and (d) records that the sampling model is the declared assumption of P7 clause (ii) and that no measured count, p-value, error rate, power, sample size or empirical conclusion is asserted. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, F1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Finite-sample threshold crossings.** At the displayed singlet settings,
  each of the four possible outcome pairs has strictly positive probability.
  A sequence with product signs $+1$ at the first three setting pairs and
  $-1$ at the last therefore has positive probability and gives
  $\widehat S=4\ge-2$. For a representable model with $S<2$, a crossing
  $\widehat S>2$ has positive probability only when its declared tables support
  at least one such sequence, as specified by clause (c); a deterministic
  table need not support one. The displayed Chebyshev upper bounds remain
  valid independently of that support condition. A finite sample on either
  side of the threshold does not by itself decide between the models; no
  optimality, power or sample-size assertion is made.
- **No inference is drawn.** The clauses are probabilities inside the declared
  sampling model. They do not compute a p-value, do not attach a confidence
  level and do not assert anything about a real experiment; the
  preparation, detection and selection qualifications remain as stated in
  [[rem-nrqm-bell-boundaries-and-comparison-scope]].

The item asserts no measured count, no p-value, no power, no error rate, no sample size and no empirical conclusion; the independence and identical distribution of trials is the declared statistical assumption of clause (ii) of P7, not a consequence of the framework.

items.title: Selection and loss: the precise hypothesis under which the CHSH bound transfers to recorded pairs
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **Recorded tables are conditional tables.** The arrangement's laws
  $\nu^{\rho}_{ij}$ of
  [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]] clause (d) describe a declared
  pair of local sign measurements for every setting pair on the declared
  preparation. A comparison with recorded data ordinarily uses only the runs
  in which both stations register an event; the laws of the recorded runs are
  therefore **conditional laws** of a larger model, and they are not the
  arrangement's tables unless a detection and selection model connecting the
  two is declared. This is part of the preparation and apparatus discipline of
  P7 clause (i) ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

- **A sufficient condition for the transfer.** If the full tables admit a
  local-response representation and the recorded runs are exactly those
  specifications lying in a measurable selection event $D$ of the
  specification space with $\mathbb P(D)>0$ — the same event for every setting
  pair, independent of the settings and of the outcomes — then the conditional
  tables again admit a local-response representation, with the same response
  laws over the conditional measure, and hence satisfy the CHSH bound
  ([[lem-nrqm-bell-setting-independent-selection-closure]]). This is the
  mathematical content of a **setting-independent detection** or
  **fair-sampling** hypothesis for the declared model class.

- **The condition is a hypothesis, not a theorem about detectors.** The
  selection-closure lemma is a conditional statement about the declared model.
  It does not assert that any laboratory detector, coincidence circuit or
  post-selection rule realizes a selection event of the required form;
  identifying a concrete apparatus with such a model is a tested
  identification with uncertainty under P7 and carries its calibration and
  control-experiment qualifications. Efficiency, dead time, misalignment,
  background and drift each require their own declared model.

- **No transfer without a selection model.** If the recorded sample is
  selected by a rule that depends on the settings or on the observed outcomes,
  the selection-closure lemma does not apply, and no claim is made here that
  the CHSH bound constrains the recorded tables. Correspondingly, a deviation
  computed from recorded pairs is a statement about those recorded tables and
  their own declared model; it becomes a statement about the full arrangement
  only through a declared selection model of the kind above. The finite-sample
  fluctuation of any such computed functional is a further, separate matter,
  treated in [[texp-nrqm-bell-finite-sample-chsh]], and the singlet contrast
  itself is the conditional model computation of
  [[texp-nrqm-bell-singlet-arrangement-contrast]].

- **Settings choice.** A test in which the settings are chosen by a procedure
  whose outcome could depend on the specification would not be described by
  one common probability law over the specification space for all setting
  pairs, which is part of the definition of a local-response representation
  ([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]] clause (c)). Randomizing or
  otherwise fixing the setting choice is a procedure-level assumption of the
  experiment's own model; this page neither assumes nor reports such a
  procedure.

items.title: Scope of the examples page: conditional computations, no experiment, and the deferred Bell-test destination
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **What the page contains.** Three conditional computations in the declared
  framework: the worked comparison at the specified directions between the
  singlet arrangement and the EPR-type product mixture, with both CHSH values
  and an explicit local-response representation of the mixture
  ([[ex-nrqm-bell-worked-angles-and-product-mixture]]); the finite-sample
  behaviour of the sample CHSH functional under a declared independent and
  identically distributed sampling model, with its concentration inequality
  and positive failure probabilities
  ([[texp-nrqm-bell-finite-sample-chsh]]); and the selection and loss
  qualification, with the precise hypothesis under which the CHSH bound
  transfers to recorded pairs
  ([[rem-nrqm-bell-selection-loss-and-fair-sampling]]).

- **What the page does not contain.** No experiment item, no reported count,
  no calibration, no detector efficiency, no loss fraction, no background
  model, no trial-level uncertainty analysis, no p-value and no confidence
  level. The worked tables, the sample functional and the failure
  probabilities are probabilities of the declared models; no number on the
  page is an observation. The identification of any apparatus with the
  declared measurements and of any repetition procedure with the declared
  sampling model is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7
  ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

- **Deferred Bell-test experiment destination.** The design of the pair
  reserves an experiment item for a Bell test. It is not built here because
  none of the sources read for the pair supplies the required trial-level
  material: a primary or authoritative full report read directly, with the
  source-specific preparation and apparatus, calibration, measured outputs,
  trial count where reported, detection efficiency, losses and
  post-selection, background, the reported statistical treatment and
  systematics, and the source's omissions. The experimental remarks of the
  secondary sources — Binney's reference to the 1972 Freedman-Clauser test
  and its citation of a 1998 photonic test, and the MIT chapter's statement
  that experiments have confirmed violations — motivate the comparison only
  and are not used as measured records; no numerical value from them is
  reproduced. The statistics and primary-report gap named in the design is
  recorded as an open destination.

- **Why a null or shifted sample is not a verdict.** The mixture's tables have
  CHSH value $-\sqrt2$ in absolute value, strictly below both the classical
  bound $2$ and the singlet's $2\sqrt2$
  ([[ex-nrqm-bell-worked-angles-and-product-mixture]]), and the finite-sample
  analysis bounds the probability that a model's sample functional crosses
  either threshold by a strictly positive quantity
  ([[texp-nrqm-bell-finite-sample-chsh]]). A finite sample therefore does not
  by itself decide between the declared models; a comparison requires the
  full battery of preparation, detection, selection and sampling assumptions,
  and agreement would be evidence about the combined assumptions, not a proof
  of the framework.

- **Model contrast is not an interpretation.** The page compares the tables of
  two declared arrangements and the class of local-response models of those
  tables ([[thm-nrqm-bell-local-representations-satisfy-chsh]]); it makes no
  claim about the completeness of quantum mechanics, about hidden variables in
  general, about mechanisms or about any interpretation of the violation. The
  boundaries of the comparison are recorded on the pair's first page.
